title: Production-Representative HPC Evaluation Contract (100 Criteria Across 4 Task Slots)
description: Machine-readable evaluation contract for onlyxItachi/perfdigest-plugin preserving 3 primary comparison arms (raw, mcp_digest, evidence), 5 separately stratified delivery strategies mapped to canonical EvidenceDelivery names, symmetric workspace write policies (read_only_diagnosis vs autonomous_patch_and_verify), answer-neutral agent output schemas, explicit automated vs blind-rubric-judge criteria, 3 confirmed real HPC workloads (75 grounded criteria), and 1 explicitly unselected Task 4 slot (25 reserved criteria).

read_only_diagnosis.description: All 3 arms (raw, mcp_digest, evidence) run strictly read-only against the clean pre-fix snapshot without editing files. Only read-only reproducer/baseline verifiers and diagnosis/design criteria apply; patch-dependent implementation verifiers are excluded from cross-arm scoring in this mode.

autonomous_patch_and_verify.description: All 3 arms (raw, mcp_digest, evidence) receive identical isolated writable copies of the clean pre-fix snapshot and symmetric shell/edit tools. Evidence arms retrieve verified Evidence via MCP pull (in_execution_tool_delivery) or the Skill-controlled OS-native background worker (skill_background_worker) rather than the read-only investigate() prompt wrapper. The external harness runs post-fix verifiers against each arm's patched workspace.

categoryTaxonomy.A: Quantitative & Profiler Evidence Grounding (exact metrics, hotspots, null != 0 honesty)
categoryTaxonomy.B: Root-Cause Localization & Mechanistic Accuracy (exact files, symbols, call paths, ABI/memory/math causes)
categoryTaxonomy.C: Correctness, Boundary & Invariant Preservation (edge cases, dtype/overflow/support/ownership/registry invariants)
categoryTaxonomy.D: Scope Honesty, Falsification & Non-Overclaiming (rejecting shortcuts/false causes, separating measured vs unproven)
categoryTaxonomy.E: Remediation Design & Independent Verification (concrete fix/disposition + external non-trivial verifier checks)

agentPrompt.taskBrief: Users report severe wall-time latency and peak-RSS memory amplification when running configured public file workflows via GAFIME dataload() on 100k x 20 and 100k x 100 CSV, Parquet, and IPC datasets compared to direct contiguous array analysis. Investigate the workspace in <SNAPSHOT_DIR> and the profiler/build artifacts in <ARTIFACT_DIR>. Identify the exact execution and memory bottlenecks, separate runtime/parser versus native memory contributions accurately, preserve all numerical, precision, and ownership contracts, and follow the run's declared workspace policy (diagnosis-only in read_only_diagnosis mode; implement and verify a patch in autonomous_patch_and_verify mode).
agentPrompt.workspaceInstructions: Use your available tools autonomously within the run's declared workspace policy (read-only vs writable). Inspect <SNAPSHOT_DIR> and staged artifacts in <ARTIFACT_DIR>. Report only directly observed metrics; set unobserved metrics to null rather than 0. Emit a single JSON object adhering strictly to outputSchema and populate measured_metrics using the declared neutralMetricKeys.

graderGroundTruth.summary: Pre-PR-#111 dataload() coupled file acquisition to a narrow explicit-Core/no-significance Arrow convenience route, forcing general configured file analyses through Polars iter_rows() and per-scalar Python validation (_append_numeric -> _finite_for_precision -> normalize_precision -> array('f') -> bytes -> Rust decode). PR #111 separated private native Arrow C Stream acquisition in crates/gafime-py/src/acquisition.rs feeding the existing full-config Rust planner/executor, cutting 100kx20 Parquet median wall from 658ms to 38.4ms and 100kx100 Parquet from 3.13s/552.5MiB to 167.7ms/247.6MiB while bounding Polars parser-floor RSS via independent-parser-v1.
rootCauses: Acquisition/execution policy coupling in python/gafime/v1_adapter.py restricted the legacy Arrow shortcut to narrow explicit-Core/no-significance matching-dtype routes.

General configured dataload() fell back to feature_frame.iter_rows() -> _coerce_row_major_f32_for_cache -> _append_numeric -> _finite_for_precision -> normalize_precision (121.8M Python calls / 10.1M scalar appends on 100kx100).
External Polars version-dependent parser/allocator floor accounted for ~114-386 MiB RSS independent of GAFIME native compile delta (~7.4-7.6 MiB fp32 / 15.1-15.2 MiB fp64 on 100kx20).
secondaryCaveats: The archived 31.8 MB docs/evidence/rt-firsthit-sm89-65536x8192-final.ncu-rep is an unrelated RT-Core GBDT capture from commit cce2839c and MUST NOT be used as an RC3 ingestion profiler artifact.
PR #114 (ab1d937) addressed a separate RC3 Core benchmark calibration headroom failure (200ms vs 220ms loop selection) and is tracked outside Task 1 unless explicitly added.

graderGroundTruth.summary: Mixed pairing of PyTorch 2.14's pybind11-era Triton (675c59878a) with nanobind-era AMD Triton-XDNA (e0667baa81) exhibits four layered incompatibilities: (1) ELF initializer symbol skew (_Z26init_triton_amd_triton_npuON8pybind117module_E vs ...RN8nanobind7module_E), (2) SIGSEGV in nanobind::detail::nb_func_new for unbootstrapped borrow-bridge shims, (3) 4-way TypeError rejection of real mlir::MLIRContext and mlir::PassManager objects across pybind11/nanobind even when both frameworks are initialized against identical LLVM 46111560, and (4) third_party/triton.patch rejection at CMakeLists.txt:327 plus LLVM pin divergence. Correct move is issue-first upstream policy clarification with AMD (not a downstream patch claiming full compatibility).
rootCauses: P1 Triton python/src/main.cc:35 expects void init_triton_amd_triton_npu(pybind11::module&&) while T1 amd_triton_npu/amd_triton_npu.cc exports void init_triton_amd_triton_npu(nanobind::module_&).
Triton commit ec2b08420d migrated to nanobind and Triton-XDNA commit 9b04876a47 adopted it; P1 and T1 embedded Triton straddle that transition.
Properly initialized pybind11 and nanobind extensions maintain disjoint native type registries and reject cross-framework MLIRContext/PassManager wrappers with TypeError.

third_party/triton.patch fails at CMakeLists.txt:327, LLVM pins diverge (46111560 vs b010a18d), and TRITON_PLUGIN_DIRS compiles OBJECT targets into host Triton rather than providing a binary plugin ABI.
secondaryCaveats: Task 2 is strictly a read_only_diagnosis upstream compatibility and reproducer task; BuildDigest traces (cmake-profile, ninja-log, clang-time-trace) complement rather than replace source/ELF/reproducer inspection.

agentPrompt.taskBrief: Mutual-information scoring and discrete split-aware candidate ranking in GAFIME produce unreliable rankings across small and large datasets: small or independent samples show inflated MI scores, skewed targets lose resolution, tiny accidental region masks receive spuriously high MI and variance-reduction scores, and the CUDA discrete selection kernel constrains target binning and shared memory poorly. Investigate <SNAPSHOT_DIR> and the staged GPU/CPU profiler and codegen artifacts in <ARTIFACT_DIR>. Diagnose the exact mathematical and cross-stack GPU/CPU/Rust defects, preserve public API stability, and follow the run's declared workspace policy (diagnosis-only in read_only_diagnosis mode; implement and verify a patch in autonomous_patch_and_verify mode).

Inspect <SNAPSHOT_DIR> and staged profiler/codegen artifacts under <ARTIFACT_DIR>. Report only directly observed metrics; set unobserved metrics to null while preserving genuine 0.0 measurements. Emit a single JSON object adhering strictly to outputSchema and populate measured_metrics using the declared neutralMetricKeys.

graderGroundTruth.summary: GAFIME v0.4.0 suffered five compounding MI defects: (1) fixed 16-bin equal-width uncorrected dense MI in cpu_metrics.py and gafime_core.cpp, (2) sparse 16x16 continuous binning of binary [0,1] region masks in discrete.py and CUDA gafime_discrete_selection_batch_kernel (1,152 B smem capped at 16 bins), (3) missing Kish effective-support guard (and fixed n_eff>=8 over-pruning small n=96 regions), (4) lack of static-capacity CUDA soft-binary templates (hist_in[B]+hist_out[B] <= 768 B at B=96) and Rust homogeneous template batching, and (5) need for safe Python fallback on legacy CUDA libraries.
rootCauses: gafime/metrics/cpu_metrics.py::mutual_info and gafime_core/src/gafime_core.cpp::build_bins + mutual_info_from_vector used fixed bins=16 equal-width histograms with no Miller-Madow finite-sample bias correction.

gafime/discrete.py::_mask_mutual_info and src/cuda/kernels.cu::gafime_discrete_selection_batch_kernel binned soft [0,1] inside/outside masks into a sparse 16x16 2D grid instead of a 2xB soft-binary contingency table.
Missing Kish effective-sample-size guard in MI and only left_weight <= 1e-9 in _soft_variance_reduction let tiny accidental regions dominate ranking.
secondaryCaveats: sklearn.feature_selection.mutual_info_regression uses a kNN estimator; exact numerical equality is NOT expected or claimed for MI (ranking agreement & monotonicity are checked, while exact equivalence is checked for VR vs tree stump and R2 vs LinearRegression).
Later v1 MI SIMD/GPU issues (#24, #44, #45) are distinct post-v0.4.1 items outside Task 3 unless explicitly added.
